Sheet.Name: Name
Sheet.DropHint: Drag an item here from a compendium.
Sheet.VehicleHint: Drag a vehicle here from the actors list to assign it to this character.

Tree.None: No archetypes yet. Add the first one.

1a.name: Dead On
1a.desc: +4 to aimed shots and aimed strikes

2a.name: Akimbo
2a.desc: With two pistols — two attacks per action, −4 to each. With two SMGs — one burst at −4: it adds 2d6 to damage instead of 1d6 and spends 10 rounds from each

2b.name: One-Two
2b.desc: Two strikes with a fist or a light weapon in one action

4b.name: Everything Is a Weapon
4b.desc: Any object in your hand — a bottle, a chair, a frying pan — is a light weapon for you, Forceful. And any light melee weapon in your hands hits like a medium one: 2d6

5a.name: Gotcha
5a.desc: A target that leaned out of cover to shoot gives you no −4 penalty

5b.name: Not Only Cowards Hit from Behind
5b.desc: A melee strike from behind or from ambush deals ×2 damage

6a.name: Duelist
6a.desc: In a one-on-one fight you act first, whatever the Initiative

7a.name: Fast Reload
7a.desc: Reloading is free, once per turn. A Slow Reload takes one action

8a.name: Eagle Eye
8a.desc: Range DCs are one step lower for you: 27 → 21, 21 → 17, 17 → 13, 13 → 9

8b.name: Bouncer
8b.desc: Every hit in melee knocks the target down

9a.name: Wall of Fire
9a.desc: Suppressing fire is a 60 m cone instead of 30

9b.name: Counterpunch
9b.desc: An enemy missed you in melee — you hit back at once, for free

1a.name: Connections
1a.desc: You know who sells what on your own city's black market — no check needed. In another city: Cool + Streetwise, DC 13

2a.name: Your Own Fence
2a.desc: Fences pay you 50% of the official price instead of 30%

2b.name: Offshore
2b.desc: The money on your card can't be seized, and debts aren't deducted from it automatically

3a.name: Another Angle
3a.desc: Failed a Deception, Persuasion or Haggling check — you may try again at once with a different approach. Once per target

4a.name: Best Friend for the Evening
4a.desc: An evening of talk, Cool + Deception against Brains + Insight: the NPC considers you a friend — shares secrets, lets you into the house. On a failure they're on their guard

4b.name: Shell Company
4b.desc: Once a month you can pay for one purchase with dirty money as if it were clean: it's put through a front company

5a.name: Lucky
5a.desc: A third Luck point per session

6a.name: Your Own Guys
6a.desc: Hiring NPC muscle costs half as much (prices — economy, section 4)

6b.name: People Are Everything
6b.desc: Workers at your businesses and rackets don't steal and don't snitch: troubles 3, 6 and 8 on the trouble table are rerolled

7a.name: At Home Anywhere
7a.desc: The “Dressed for the Part” penalties don't apply to you: you fit in anywhere (economy, section 3)

7b.name: Hostile Takeover
7b.desc: Once a month, Brains + Business, DC 21: someone else's business becomes yours for half its price. On paper it's all clean

8a.name: Just Passing By
8a.desc: As long as you haven't fired a shot or thrown a punch, witnesses don't remember you: no wanted level is called on you

8b.name: Board of Directors
8b.desc: One manager of an illegal racket works for 0%. The others are more agreeable: talking their cut down is one step easier

9a.name: Man Without a Past
9a.desc: Once a month you can change your identity for free: documents, looks, cover story. Your wanted level resets, witnesses no longer recognize you

9b.name: Your Own Company
9b.desc: Your own business brings in twice the profit

10a.name: The Greatest Con
10a.desc: A fourth Luck point. After a reroll you choose either of the results

1a.name: Golden Hands
1a.desc: You make repairs yourself and for free: armor in 1 hour, Brains + Electronics, DC 13; a car with no money for parts

1b.name: City on the Line
1b.desc: An action, Brains + Computers, DC 13: within 50 m, open or lock an electronic door, an elevator or a barrier, or switch a traffic light. Guarded systems — DC 17

2a.name: Do It Yourself
2a.desc: You build any item from the gear and weapon lists using the “Assembly” rules

2b.name: Phone Hack
2b.desc: Brains + Computers, DC 17. A phone within 50 m — an action; by number — 10 minutes. Until the end of the day you read its messages, listen to its calls and see where the phone is

3a.name: Inventor
3a.desc: Using “Assembly” you create your own items that aren't on the lists, and your own weapons

3b.name: Eyes in the Cameras
3b.desc: An action, Brains + Computers, DC 17: you see through every camera within 50 m and erase the recordings. An erased camera is no witness

4a.name: Upgrade
4a.desc: Raise a weapon's quality by one step: a week of work, Brains + Gunsmithing, DC 17, parts cost half the price

4b.name: Backdoor
4b.desc: A device you have hacked even once stays open. You get into it from anywhere in the city without a roll until the owner replaces the device

5a.name: Garage Genius
5a.desc: You fit vehicle modifications yourself — in an hour and at half price

5b.name: Admin Rights
5b.desc: The DC of your hacking actions is one step lower: 21 → 17, 17 → 13, 13 → 9

6a.name: Demolition Man
6a.desc: The blast zone of your bombs and charges is one step larger (6 × 6 → 10 × 10 m)

6b.name: Digital Trail
6b.desc: Once a month, erase one piece of evidence in the FBI agent's file from the databases

7a.name: Sapper
7a.desc: Your bombs and charges don't go off early

7b.name: Ghost
7b.desc: Cameras don't capture you. Your outline is always blurred on them

8a.name: Spit and Duct Tape
8a.desc: An action: a broken or destroyed item works for 10 more minutes — a car at 0 HP drives, a smashed phone makes calls

8b.name: Botnet
8b.desc: Hacking abilities that work within 50 m work anywhere in the city for you

9a.name: Gold Standard
9a.desc: Everything you build is of Fine quality or gets one extra property for free. Worse only if you want it to be

9b.name: Blackout
9b.desc: An action, DC 21: lights, comms and cameras go out across the block. The darkness holds as long as you spend every following turn on this action. While it's dark nobody can reach 911 and the wanted level doesn't rise

1a.name: Your Own Audience
1a.desc: Your releases bring in followers — see the “Audience” rules above

2a.name: Source
2a.desc: When you dig into someone or something, the GM gives you at least one confirmed fact whatever the roll

2b.name: Fans
2b.desc: Once per session a fan helps with something small: gives you a lift, puts you up for the night, distracts a cop

3a.name: Press Pass
3a.desc: At ⭐ the cops check your papers and let you go

4a.name: Spin
4a.desc: Any release can be made into spin, DC 17: a person's or a business's reputation goes one step up or down. Such a release brings no followers. On a failure nothing happens

4b.name: Fan Club
4b.desc: Once per session 2d6 fans gather wherever you say. They won't fight

5a.name: Content Machine
5a.desc: Two releases a week instead of one

6a.name: Leak
6a.desc: Once a month a release can be made into a leak about a business or a racket, DC 17: this month it earns nothing — inspections, searches, reporters at the door

6b.name: Devoted
6b.desc: Fans break the law in small ways for you: lie to cops, hide things, testify in your favor

7a.name: Fourth Estate
7a.desc: “Spin” can be aimed at a cop, a judge, an official or an FBI agent. At a “Shady” reputation they get −2 to all checks against you and your gang; at “Disgrace” — −4

7b.name: Fan Security
7b.desc: Once per session 2d6 fans stand up for you: they fight with whatever they have — usually fists and bats, though someone will have a gun — and shield you with their bodies

8a.name: Scoop
8a.desc: A “Spin” release also brings in followers

8b.name: Idol
8b.desc: +4 to Persuasion against those who know you

9a.name: High-Profile Case
9a.desc: Once a month, Brains + Deduction, DC 17: the FBI agent handling you is taken off the case, and the new one gets only half the file. On a failure nothing happens

9b.name: Anything for the Idol
9b.desc: Once per session a fan carries out one serious errand: steal a car, lift an item, beat someone up. If caught, they won't give you up

10a.name: The Cameraman Never Dies
10a.desc: While you're streaming or filming, nobody opens fire on you unless you shot first

1a.name: Call It In
1a.desc: You call the cops — see the “Calling the cops” rules above

2a.name: Badge
2a.desc: The badge passes a cop check: they treat you as an ally as long as you don't break the law or enter guarded premises

2b.name: Attorney–Client Privilege
2b.desc: Wiretaps and recordings of your conversations don't become evidence against you or your clients

3a.name: Anonymous Tip
3a.desc: Once per session, put the police onto a competitor: they get ⭐⭐ and a search

4a.name: Friends at the Precinct
4a.desc: Once per session, find out what the cops know about a case: evidence, suspects, wanted level

4b.name: Your Own Judge
4b.desc: Bribing a judge costs half as much — for a lenient sentence or a harsh one

5a.name: Released on Recognizance
5a.desc: Someone arrested at ⭐⭐⭐ can be bailed out — $1,000 per wanted level, as at ⭐–⭐⭐

6a.name: Service Issue
6a.desc: A gun and a vest from the precinct. The weapon is Registered to the precinct: the bullets lead there

6b.name: Inadmissible Evidence
6b.desc: Once a month one piece of evidence in the FBI agent's file against you or a client disappears

7a.name: Backup
7a.desc: The cops you call in follow your orders

7b.name: Prison Mail
7b.desc: You know who to talk to in any prison, and the prices are fixed. Against someone inside: $1,000 to pass on a message or an item, $5,000 for a beating (4d6 damage), $20,000 to have them removed

8a.name: Warrant
8a.desc: Once per session, a search of a target: the cops seize everything illegal, and every find is evidence against them

8b.name: Reasonable Doubt
8b.desc: When you defend yourself or a client in court, each piece of evidence gives the defense −1 instead of −2

9a.name: Blue Wall
9a.desc: As long as you have no more than ⭐⭐, the cops don't arrest you: they don't give up their own

9b.name: Appeal
9b.desc: A lost trial — yours or a client's — can be appealed: the defense roll is repeated. Once per case

10a.name: I Am the Law
10a.desc: Once per session, put a person on the wanted list: they get ⭐⭐⭐ and the cops look for them all over the city

10b.name: Forewarned
10b.desc: You learn of an arrest or search warrant against you or a client a day ahead. If another player's ability sends a warrant, a search or a wanted level your way, it takes effect only a day later, and you know about it at once

Adv.Title: Advancement: {name}
Adv.OpenHint: Spend XP on skills and development points. The badge shows unspent XP.
Adv.EarnedHint: XP earned in play. The starting 1000 XP for skills is not included.
Adv.StatsNote: 25 points across four stats, each from 2 to 10. HP = 10 + Muscle × 2.
Adv.StatsLocked: Stats don't grow with XP: they can be changed only during character creation.
Adv.SkillsNote: Level N costs N × 10 XP. Basic skills start at 2 for free (in brackets), your native language at 4, English at 2. The right column shows XP already spent on the skill. Shift — two levels at once.
Adv.ArchNote: One development point — one ability. Three points are free (at creation: 3 in one archetype or 2 and 1), each next one costs 100 XP. A level opens once an ability of the previous level is taken; OR closes the other path.

NoName.sciences: A science with a level has no name
NoName.instruments: An instrument with a level has no name

Adv.OneNative: Exactly one native language is needed
Adv.Scheme: At creation the three points go 3 in one archetype or 2 and 1

1.problem: Neighbors complain about the noise, the smell and the odd visitors
1.solve: $500 to the neighbors or Cool + Persuasion, DC 13

2.solve: $2,000 for parts or Brains + Electronics, DC 17

3.problem: A worker is stealing product or takings
3.solve: Find out who: Brains + Insight, DC 13. What to do with them is your call

4.solve: Find a new one: Cool + Streetwise, DC 17. Or find out who bought off the old one

5.solve: A bribe from $2,000 or get rid of whatever he noticed

6.problem: A worker quit and talks too much
6.solve: Find them and make them keep quiet: money, threats or something worse

7.problem: A local gang wants a cut
7.solve: Pay 20% of the income every month or talk to the gang another way: a fight

8.solve: Get them out: bail and a lawyer. Or make sure they don't talk

9.problem: A journalist is working on a story
9.solve: Buy them, scare them or slip them a juicier story

10.problem: Competitors cleaned the place out: product and takings are gone
10.solve: Take it back: a raid on the competitors

11.solve: A bribe from $5,000 or destroy the evidence

12.problem: War: competitors want the whole market
12.solve: Skirmishes and raids until one side gives up or runs out

13.problem: Raid: the police or the FBI are preparing a bust
13.solve: One week to move the equipment and cover the tracks. Too late — the racket is lost, and everyone caught on site gets three wanted stars
